analysis: What changed vs the 9 AM brief Wednesday: the story is no longer the morning flush — it is the reversal. The Dow erased a 1,100-point loss to finish green, the S&P clawed back from -3.2% intraday to -0.25%, and the Nasdaq from -4.6% to -0.62%, with the Nasdaq-100 briefly touching bear-market territory (-20% from its early-October peak) before recovering. The genuinely new overnight items are the Bank of Korea's 25bp hike to 3.25% (5-2, growth forecasts raised on the chip boom) and the Houthi-claimed strike on the Ras Tanura refinery lifting Brent to $94.61 — both reinforce the inflation/rates pressure that helped start the selloff, even as equities bounced. Trump's floated US stake in Nvidia (NY Post interview, confirmed across outlets) is the other carried item: no proposal exists, but it adds a policy overhang to the stock that defines the AI trade, and NVDA is still 37.6% below its October closing high despite being up 18.9% on the week. Asia's rebound (Nikkei +1.5%, Kospi +1.8%, Taiex +2.9%) and higher US futures say the dip-buying has follow-through for now. Signal vs noise: the intraday reversal on heavy volume, the VIX settling at 28.29 after topping 30, the concrete BoK hike and the oil jump are signal; any single futures print on a holiday morning and the Trump stake trial balloon are noise until something is actually proposed. With markets closed today and a half-day Friday, the risk is thin holiday tape amplifying the first move in either direction. No qualifying Hacker News or Reddit threads added signal beyond the headlines this morning, so community_signals is empty.

headlines.headline: Markets closed for Thanksgiving; US index futures higher early Thursday — Dow +0.4%, S&P 500 +0.55%, Nasdaq-100 +0.55% — extending Wednesday's late-session rebound.
headlines.why_it_matters: Futures are carrying the dip-buying momentum into the holiday pause — a steadier setup for Friday's thin half session, though overnight futures do not guarantee Friday's open.

headlines.headline: Wednesday's wild reversal: Dow erased a 1,100+ point intraday loss to close +0.33% at 50,182.95; S&P 500 -0.25% to 7,182.78 after falling as much as 3.2%; Nasdaq -0.62% to 23,585.80 after falling as much as 4.6%, with the Nasdaq-100 briefly ~20% below its early-October peak. Russell 2000 +0.71%, its third straight gain.
headlines.why_it_matters: Dip-buyers stepped in hard in the afternoon, but the indexes are still inside last week's range and volatility is very high — a reversal, not a confirmed turn.

headlines.headline: Asian markets rebound Thursday: Nikkei +1.5%, Kospi +1.8%, Taiwan Taiex +2.9%, Hang Seng +2.0%, Shanghai +0.1%, led by the chip names that sold off hardest Wednesday.
headlines.why_it_matters: Global dip-buying is following Wall Street's late recovery — a steadier backdrop for Friday's reopen, with the rebound still modest next to Wednesday's slide (Kospi fell 6.2% Wednesday).

headlines.headline: Bank of Korea hikes 25bp to 3.25% (5-2 vote), its third hike since July and highest since Nov 2024, citing the AI-driven chip export boom and elevated inflation; raises 2026 growth forecast to 3.9% (from 3.3%) and 2027 to 4.1% (from 2.9%).
headlines.why_it_matters: A major central bank is tightening into the AI boom — it reinforces the higher-for-longer rates backdrop that is pressuring growth stocks, even as the hike was widely expected.

headlines.headline: Trump told the New York Post it is 'probably not too late' for a US government equity stake in Nvidia, like the ~10% stake taken in Intel last year, and said he would pardon CEO Jensen Huang if needed — but no proposal has been made and it has not been raised with the company. NVDA closed $149.30 (-3.9%) Wednesday, up 18.9% for the week and 37.6% below its Oct 6 closing high.
headlines.why_it_matters: Even as a trial balloon, a government stake puts state priorities into the most-watched chip stock — an overhang on the multiple — while the Dec 1/3 congressional hearings are still ahead. Earnings context: Nov 17, EPS $2.68 vs $2.47 expected, revenue $115.84B vs $109.28B expected (+103% y/y).

headlines.headline: Oil jumps on a Houthi-claimed attack on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery: Brent +3.51% to $94.61, WTI +1.99% to $83.68.
headlines.why_it_matters: A supply-risk premium in crude adds to the inflation backdrop the Fed is watching into the Dec 8-9 meeting, where a hike is now priced near-certain after hot October core PCE (3.3%).

headlines.headline: November's Mag 7 scorecard: Apple is the month's winner (+3.3%, fifth straight monthly gain, now nearly $2T more valuable than Microsoft); Nvidia is the worst performer at a $3.6T market cap. Drawdowns from highs: NVDA -37.6% from its Oct 6 close, GOOGL -32.2% from its May 13 peak, META -22.8%, TSLA -22.4%, AMZN -13.9%, MSFT -11.9%; Apple just -0.2% below its Nov 13 close. Wednesday closes: META +3.4% to $609.89, AAPL +0.4% to $355.58, MSFT -1.25% to $489.93, AMZN -3.1% to $244.43, GOOGL -2.0% to $270.98, TSLA -1.2% to $380.14.
headlines.why_it_matters: The month's rotation out of AI leaders into Apple and defensives is the story of the tape — leadership has flipped, and the most AI-exposed names are down most.

headlines.headline: Anthropic (ANT) reverses from a record low of $73.85 to close $82.79 (+1.1%), just under its $83 IPO price and ~28% below its $115 opening-day high.
headlines.why_it_matters: The $80 level held and the IPO is nearly back to its issue price — a small stabilization signal for the AI complex, but the bounce is modest against the week's damage.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC news overnight. Carry-forward: Zacks raised its FY2026 EPS estimate to $1.16 from $1.04 (Nov 24), FY2027 at $1.31; a Seeking Alpha analysis calls USAC a buy at $23.63, citing the 8.9% yield backed by 1.67x distribution coverage and record pricing. Units traded ~$23.14 Wednesday, near the 52-week low of $22.65. Q3 2026 (Nov 3): revenue $357.2M (+43% y/y, above ~$348.3M consensus), EPS $0.33/unit in line, adjusted EBITDA $197.3M, DCF $127.1M, coverage 1.67x; FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance narrowed to $770-780M; $0.525/unit quarterly distribution (annualized $2.10) paid Nov 6; $500M order book through 2029, >60% of 2027 new horsepower contracted. Next earnings Feb 16, 2027.
